name: bt6-platform-host
title: Build targets stage 6: the platform layer (window, lifecycle, loop ownership, input sources, paths) with desktop-glfw, headless and web backends; web-stubs' fake GLFW removed
issue: User request, 2026-11-10: 'I would like for the engine to be able to allow the user to select a build target in the engine editor UI like windows, linux, android, ios, web, and maybe other console toolchains in the future like switch'. Design and stage table: orchestrator/proposals/build-targets-design.md. Stage 6 of section 5.
acceptance: engine/ outside the desktop-glfw backend includes no GLFW header
Window.cpp and the web player run on the platform layer; lifecycle events exist and are tested with a fake backend
No behaviour change: full tests, smoke plans, the web package smoke and the web budgets pass
A headless backend (no window: the editor host, n2server, the test suites, the golden replay and determinism legs) keeps working, with its own tests
gate: needs the user's go; depends on bt5-engine-input-codes
notes: Reviewer: the interface is enough for Android and iOS (lifecycle, surface loss, insets, loop owned by the OS) without changing it later. The headless backend is not an afterthought: the editor host and CI run without a window.
